name: Isolated Exencephaly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Exencephaly

criteria.description: Presence of a cranial neural tube defect characterized by absence of the calvarium with exposed disorganized brain tissue
Radiologic confirmation of absent cranial vault (calvarium) on prenatal ultrasound or MRI
No associated major anomalies or syndromic features detected

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of cranial neural tube defect with absent calvarium and exposed brain tissue confirmed by imaging, without other major anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is typically made prenatally by ultrasound or MRI; postnatal confirmation is rare due to lethality.

imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing absent cranial vault with exposed brain tissue
Fetal MRI confirming absence of calvarium and disorganized cerebral tissue
other: Postmortem examination confirms absence of skull bones and exposed brain tissue

distinguishingFeatures: Complete absence of brain tissue and cranial vault versus presence of disorganized brain tissue in exencephaly
Anencephaly is more advanced neural tube defect with absent cerebral hemispheres
Presence of skull defect with herniation of brain tissue covered by skin or meninges
Exencephaly involves absent calvarium with exposed brain tissue, not covered

redFlags: Absent cranial vault with exposed brain tissue on prenatal imaging
Severe craniofacial malformations incompatible with life
references: Copp AJ, et al. Neural tube defects: recent advances, unsolved questions, and controversies. Lancet Neurol. 2013 Aug;12(8):799-810.
Moore KL, Persaud TVN. The Developing Human: Clinically Oriented Embryology. 11th Edition. Elsevier; 2015.
